title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, stop a fixed-width truncation from cutting a file path in h
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts, stop a fixed-width truncation from cutting a file path in half.

The file contains exactly one occurrence of this fragment, on line 2670:
.slice(0, 400),

Replace that one fragment with exactly this text:
.slice(0, 400).replace(/^.{400}$/s, (m) => m.replace(/\s\S*$/, "")),

Copy the replacement character for character. It contains exactly four closing parentheses and ends with the five characters "")), — a previous attempt at this same edit dropped a parenthesis near the end and failed typecheck with TS1005 at line 2670 column 300, so the parenthesis balance is the thing to get right. Change nothing else on the line, no other line, and no other file. This is a suffix appended to an existing call: the text before .slice(0, 400) stays exactly as it is.

WHY. That line builds a child-gap goal as a 102-character prefix plus parentSummary.slice(0, 400). Measured today on gap route-edit-098185ac: 102 + 400 produced a summary of exactly 502 characters and the cut landed inside a file extension, turning the real path repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/learning-signal-health-observer.ts into learning-signal-health-observer.t, one character short. That truncated string was stored as classification_metadata.edit_site, so a compose was routed at a file that does not exist, examined 0 of 1 staged files, and broke rung 2 of the operational_state ladder.

The new code is a no-op whenever no truncation happened: the regex matches only when the sliced string is exactly 400 characters, which occurs only when the slice actually cut something. In that case it drops the trailing partial token so the text ends on a complete word instead of mid-path. The s flag is required because summaries contain newlines. A single token longer than 400 characters is left alone rather than emptied. Verified by execution against the real failing string before dispatch.
